title: Hopfield reservoir for Mirror address bank
hypothesis: Modern Hopfield retrieval of binary Mirror addresses recovers corrupted view codes with lower total address bytes than an explicit packed table while retaining decoded function quality and limiting interference as bank size grows.
physical_object: one shared linear view decoder and address bank
mirror_coordinate: 8D view code selected by a 32-bit binary address attractor
logical_multiplicity: K logical linear functions, K in {16,64,256}, measured by decoded-view quality and retrieval accuracy

development.selection_metric: exact view recovery, decoded nMSE, collisions, actual bytes, lookup MACs

storage.authority: actual serialized ZIP/NPY inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: At K=64 and 256: >=99% exact recovery for <=2 bit flips, decoded nMSE <=1e-4, >=10% fewer total bytes than packed explicit table, and query MAC <= explicit lookup.
failure_gate: Storage saving <10%, Hamming control matches recovery, quality fails, or Hopfield compute >1.1x Hamming; fresh sealed.
boundaries: synthetic random binary attractors and fixed decoder
attractor count is not model capacity
